title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Strictly Regulating the Extension of Trial Period and Adjournment of Hearings in Civil and Commercial Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 1: When hearing civil and commercial cases, the People's Court shall strictly abide by the provisions of laws and judicial interpretations on adjudication periods. For first-instance cases tried under the ordinary procedure, the adjudication period shall be six months; for first-instance cases tried under the summary procedure, the adjudication period shall be three months. For appeals against judgments, the adjudication period shall be three months; for appeals against rulings, the adjudication period shall be thirty days.
Where there are special circumstances requiring an extension of the adjudication period as provided by law, the sole judge or the collegial panel shall file an application with the president of the court fifteen days before the expiration of the period, and explain the detailed circumstances and reasons. The president shall make a decision five days before the expiration of the period.
After the extension approved by the president of the court, if the case still cannot be concluded and a further extension is needed, the matter shall be reported to the higher People's Court for approval fifteen days before the expiration of the period. The higher People's Court shall make a decision five days before the expiration of the adjudication period.

Article 2: The "other circumstances that warrant an adjournment" as provided in item (4) of Article 146 of the Civil Procedure Law refer to circumstances where the court hearing cannot be conducted normally due to force majeure or unexpected incidents.

Article 3: The People's Court shall strictly limit the number of adjournments of hearings. For civil and commercial cases tried under the ordinary procedure, the number of hearing adjournments shall not exceed two; for civil and commercial cases tried under the summary procedure and the small-claim speedy procedure, the number of hearing adjournments shall not exceed one.

Article 4: Primary People's Courts and their dispatched tribunals shall apply the summary procedure to simple civil and commercial cases with clear facts, definite rights and obligations, and minor disputes.
Primary People's Courts and their dispatched tribunals shall apply the summary procedure to civil and commercial cases that meet the requirements of the preceding paragraph and where the amount in controversy is not more than twice the average annual wage of employed persons in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government in the previous year, except for cases to which the summary procedure does not apply as provided by laws and judicial interpretations.
For civil and commercial cases tried under the summary procedure, pre-trial procedures such as evidence exchange and pre-trial conferences shall be conducted together with the hearing, and shall not be organized separately.
For cases applying the summary procedure, service by public announcement shall not apply.

Article 5: After a People's Court has held a hearing on a civil and commercial case, if it considers that an adjournment of the hearing is necessary, it shall, in accordance with law, inform the parties of the time of the next hearing. The interval between the two hearings shall not exceed one month, except for reasons of force majeure or with the consent of the parties.
Article 6: Where a sole judge or a collegial panel decides to adjourn a hearing under item (4) of Article 146 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall report to the president of the court for approval.

Article 7: The People's Court shall, in accordance with the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Publicizing Trial Process Information by the People's Courts via the Internet, promptly disclose to the parties and their statutory agents and litigation agents the case filing time, adjudication period, any deduction, extension, or recalculation of the adjudication period, and the circumstances of and reasons for adjournment of hearings. Where the parties and their statutory agents or litigation agents object, they may, in accordance with law, apply to the court accepting the case for supervision.

Article 8: Where a person intentionally delays case handling in violation of laws, adjudication discipline, or adjudication management rules, or negligently delays case handling and thereby causes serious consequences, he or she shall be disciplined in accordance with Article 47 of the Regulations on Punishment of Personnel of the People's Courts.

Article 9: These Provisions shall come into force on April 26, 2018. Where any judicial interpretations or normative documents previously issued by the Supreme People's Court are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
